thread:
Marta: Hey infra — quick one. I only have a trace_id from the error page (trace: 4fa3b2...). What's the fastest way to pull the full request payload + raw log lines? console trace view isn't showing the x-request-id for this one.
Ian: If console trace has spans, click the span that points to the ingress/edge, then use the "Open logs" link. But if sampling dropped the request you won't see the x-req header.
Marta: Right, I tried that and it's empty for this trace. Want to avoid spinning up a full grep across clusters.
Ian: Try the CLI quick path first:
```
# attempt 1: direct trace->logs helper (our infra cli)
rwdctl observability find-logs --trace 4fa3b2 --window 2m
```
That hits the trace index and returns any correlated log lines. If that returns nothing, next step:
```
# fallback: search ingress logs for span -> request header
kubectl -n infra logs -l app=edge-proxy --since=5m | grep "4fa3b2" -A4 -B2
```
Tyler: Another useful pattern: search log storage for the traceid, then extract x-request-ref or x-request-id from nearby lines and re-run an ID search. In ES/Kibana query: `trace.id:"4fa3b2" OR message:"4fa3b2"`.
devops-bot: Automated hint: there's a saved dashboard "trace -> raw logs (edge->svc)" for quick lookups: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/trace-raw-logs
Marta: Nice link, thanks. If rwdctl find-logs still misses it, how do we hunt for payloads?
Ian: Payloads are only logged at the svc level (customer-data-service) for debug builds. If you have a request id (x-req) you can pull raw pod logs: `kubectl logs <pod> -c app | grep "x-req: abcd1234" -A20`. If all else fails, check the ingress raw request capture in the edge-proxy s3 bucket (we rotate fast).
Nina: FYI we recently lowered tracing sampling to 0.1 in prod — that explains gaps. If this trace is important for a regression, we can temporarily bump sampling to 1.0 for the 5m window and re-run the request. (Security team ok with short window?) :thinking_face:
Tyler: Security ok with short window for debug sessions if requested via ticket. For future, add a quick trace->req-id enrichment in our pipeline so trace hits always write the x-req to the trace index. Filing a follow-up ticket.
Marta: Cool. For now I'll run `rwdctl observability find-logs` and fall back to kubectl greps and S3 edge captures. Thanks all :thumbsup:
